questions.text: According to PHIVOLCS guidelines, what is the minimum setback distance required from an active fault trace for inhabited structures?

options.text: 3 meters, same as PD 1067 stream easements
5 meters minimum setback
20 meters, same as PD 1067 river easements
No setback required if the structure is earthquake-resistant

rationale.a: Student confuses fault setback with water body easement distance
rationale.b: PHIVOLCS requires a 5-meter minimum setback from active fault traces—this is a seismic hazard standard, not a water-based easement.
rationale.d: Student incorrectly assumes engineering design eliminates locational hazard
rationale.correct: PHIVOLCS requires a 5-meter minimum setback from active fault traces—this is a seismic hazard standard, not a water-based easement.
rationale.takeaway: Fault setback (5m) is different from water easements (3m, 20m, 40m).

questions.text: A proposed mixed-use development is planned for a 4-hectare site in Quezon City. The site analysis reveals: (1) the site slopes toward an estero 300 meters downslope; (2) the water table is 2 meters below grade during the dry season and rises to near-surface during monsoon; (3) the site borders a small protected mangrove area to the west; and (4) the 25-year flood elevation is 0.8 meters above current site grade. The planner must determine if this site is ecologically and hydrologically feasible for mixed-use development. Which of the following represents the most comprehensive analysis?

options.text: The mangrove constraint alone makes the site unsuitable; recommend site abandonment, as the ecological impact would be too significant to mitigate effectively

Development is feasible if buildings are elevated above the 25-year flood level, impervious surfaces are minimized to maintain infiltration, the mangrove is preserved as a buffer for both flood absorption and habitat protection, and a geotechnical investigation addresses foundation design in high water table conditions
The flood risk is too great; elevate all structures 5 meters above grade and fill the surrounding site to create developable land, ensuring that all potential water ingress points are sealed

Ground water and flooding are engineering problems, not planning constraints; proceed with standard site development and let the engineer address hazards during design, assuming that all necessary adjustments can be made post-construction

rationale.a: Student treats single constraint as total prohibition
rationale.b: Comprehensive analysis integrates flood elevation, water table, and mangrove preservation—development is feasible with design adaptations that respect all constraints simultaneously.
rationale.c: Student adopts expensive mitigation without considering alternatives or ecological impacts
rationale.d: Student defers ecological and hydrological analysis to design phase
rationale.correct: Comprehensive analysis integrates flood elevation, water table, and mangrove preservation—development is feasible with design adaptations that respect all constraints simultaneously.
rationale.takeaway: Integrate flood, water table, and ecological constraints; adapt design accordingly.

The site has significant flood risk; development should elevate sensitive uses above the 25-year flood level, preserve or restore the mangrove for flood buffering, and potentially integrate detention areas on the site
Mangrove preservation is an environmental concern, not a site planning concern; commercial development can proceed at grade level, assuming standard flood precautions are in place

questions.text: A site planner is preparing a comprehensive ecological analysis for a proposed 10-hectare residential development in a barangay near a river. The site contains degraded secondary growth, slopes of 10–20 degrees (moderate), and the river runs along the southern boundary. During preliminary ecological assessment, the planner identifies three overlapping constraints: (1) PD 1067 easement from the river (planner must determine applicable distance based on hydrologic surveys showing river width of approximately 7 meters); (2) presence of bird species that migrate through the site seasonally; and (3) high groundwater table (1.5 meters below grade in dry season). The planner must decide how to integrate these findings into a preliminary development strategy that respects ecological limits while testing feasibility. Which approach most appropriately balances ecological integrity with development feasibility?

options.text: Recommend abandoning the site because all three constraints make development impossible, which is a conservative approach but may not consider innovative solutions

Ignore the migratory bird habitat because it is a seasonal use, not permanent; focus only on the PD 1067 easement (20 meters for a 7-meter river) and foundation design for high water table; this narrows constraints to manageable levels, though it may overlook ecological impacts

Document all three constraints, establish a 20-meter no-build zone from the river per PD 1067, identify development zones outside the easement and outside seasonal bird-use areas, design for high water table with appropriate foundations, and recommend preservation of riparian vegetation and some degraded areas as connectivity corridors—feasibility depends on whether the reduced developable area meets the project's economic requirements
The migratory birds and river easement are environmental concerns requiring a full EIA; site planning cannot proceed without DENR's ECC approval, which is a necessary step for compliance

rationale.a: Student conflates overlapping constraints with total prohibition
rationale.b: Student dismisses ecological constraints as less important than physical buildability
rationale.c: Comprehensive site planning documents all constraints, respects easements and habitat, and identifies reduced developable areas while testing economic viability—this is responsible planning.
rationale.d: Student conflates site planning's responsibility (to note ecological constraints) with DENR's responsibility (to conduct EIA and issue ECC)
rationale.correct: Comprehensive site planning documents all constraints, respects easements and habitat, and identifies reduced developable areas while testing economic viability—this is responsible planning.
rationale.takeaway: Integrate all constraints; identify reduced but viable development zones; assess feasibility.

Site planning must conduct the full EIA and prepare the ECC application, ensuring all environmental impacts are thoroughly assessed
ECAs and EIAs are the same thing and site planners handle both comprehensively, which may lead to confusion in regulatory compliance
If a site is in an ECA, site planning is impossible and the site must be abandoned, which may not be a feasible approach for all projects

rationale.a: Site planning notes constraints (ECA designation); DENR specialists conduct full EIA and issue ECC. These are ALE-PLAN-004-02 vs. ALE-PLAN-005-03 roles.

rationale.takeaway: Planners flag ECAs; DENR conducts EIA and issues ECC.

questions.text: A proposed residential development is planned for a barangay that borders a river. The river is approximately 8 meters wide. The site planner must assess PD 1067 (Water Code) constraints on the development. Based on the river width, what is the relevant easement distance, and what is the site planner's responsibility in site analysis?

options.text: The easement is 3 meters because all rivers require a 3-meter setback; the site planner enforces this setback in the site plan

The easement is 20 meters (for rivers ≥6m wide); the site planner documents this constraint in the site analysis and marks it as no-build; full legal enforcement belongs to the permitting stage and ALE-PLAN-005-03
The easement distance varies year-to-year with water flow and cannot be determined in site planning, which complicates long-term development strategies
PD 1067 easements are environmental law and not relevant to physical site planning analysis, though they may impact legal compliance

rationale.a: Student applies the smaller easement distance regardless of river width classification
rationale.b: PD 1067 specifies 20m easement for rivers ≥6m wide; site planners note this constraint; legal enforcement is ALE-PLAN-005-03 scope.
rationale.c: Student misunderstands that easement distance is fixed by law, not variable with hydrology
rationale.d: Student separates regulatory constraints from site planning
rationale.correct: PD 1067 specifies 20m easement for rivers ≥6m wide; site planners note this constraint; legal enforcement is ALE-PLAN-005-03 scope.
rationale.takeaway: Planners flag PD 1067 easements; lawyers enforce them at permitting stage.

questions.text: In coastal areas following the post-Typhoon Yolanda National Zoning Framework (2014), what is the no-build zone distance from mean high tide?

options.text: 20 meters
40 meters from mean high tide
5 meters (same as fault setback)
No restriction; coastal development is permitted at any distance

rationale.a: Student confuses the coastal no-build zone with PD 1067 river easement
rationale.b: Post-Haiyan coastal protection requires 40-meter no-build zone from mean high tide to provide evacuation space and reduce storm surge risk.
rationale.c: Student conflates coastal hazard zone with seismic setback
rationale.d: Student is unfamiliar with post-disaster coastal regulation
rationale.correct: Post-Haiyan coastal protection requires 40-meter no-build zone from mean high tide to provide evacuation space and reduce storm surge risk.
rationale.takeaway: Coastal no-build = 40m (post-Yolanda); different from fault (5m) and river (3/20/40m per type) setbacks.
